summary.text: Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 42, in office since January 2015. An engineer, investment banker and former math teacher by background, she is the Assembly Majority Whip, chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight of Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs), and has also served as chair of the Kings County Democratic Party. She is running for re-election in November 2026.

paragraphs.text: Bichotte Hermelyn was born and raised in Flatbush, Brooklyn, the daughter of Haitian immigrants; according to her official biography, she is the first Haitian American woman elected in New York City. The biography also says she attended LaGuardia School of Music and Performing Arts.

She holds an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management, an MS in electrical engineering from Illinois Institute of Technology, a BS in electrical engineering from SUNY Buffalo, and a BS in mathematics in secondary education and a BT in electrical engineering from Buffalo State College; the biography says she graduated from Brooklyn Law School in 2024 with a J.D.

Before public office, she worked as a math teacher in the New York City public school system, a telecommunications engineer (with assignments in Japan and China), and an investment banker, according to her official biography, and was named an MIT Fellow in the Mel King Co-Lab Project.
She was elected a Democratic District Leader in 2010 and served as a board member of Habitat for Humanity, taking part in a 2011 home-building effort in Leogane, Haiti, according to the biography.

Bichotte Hermelyn ran for the District 42 Assembly seat in 2014, defeating three candidates in the Democratic primary, and assumed office on January 1, 2015, succeeding Rhoda Jacobs. Since becoming a legislator she has introduced more than 200 bills, 34 of which have become law, and co-sponsored more than 250 others, according to her official biography.

She serves as Assembly Majority Whip and chairs the MWBE oversight subcommittee, which her biography credits with sponsored laws enacted in 2022 on MWBE program fraud, refinancing through the MWBE lending program and state contract spending thresholds; she also sits on the Housing, Education, Governmental Operations, Health, Higher Education and Ways and Means committees.

She sponsored the Jonah Bichotte Cowan Law, named for her late son, which sets requirements for hospital treatment of women who come in with concerns about pre-term labor. Her biography also describes her role in establishing the Haitian Studies Institute at Brooklyn College and the Little Haiti Cultural and Business District in Flatbush.

She was nominated chair of the Kings County Democratic County Committee in January 2020, according to Ballotpedia. In October 2026, City & State reported that a state Supreme Court justice ruled her term as chair of the Brooklyn Democratic Party's executive committee ended after a September 23 organizational meeting.
Bichotte Hermelyn sits on Governor Kathy Hochul's Domestic Violence Advisory Council and lives in Brooklyn with her husband, Edu Hermelyn, and their son, according to her official biography.
